intro: A few things that have changed in the last couple of years. Check the sources linked on each item for full details.

items.title: Busiest Everest spring season on record
items.text: By 24 May, 879 climbers and guides had reached the summit from the Nepal side, with roughly 75 more expected, and a record 494 permits had been issued. A record 274 people summited on a single day, 20 May.

items.title: Kami Rita Sherpa climbs Everest for the 32nd time
items.text: Kami Rita extended his own record on 17 May. On the same day Lhakpa Sherpa reached the top for the 11th time, the most for any woman.

items.title: New Khumbu Icefall fee and stricter waste rules
items.text: Foreign climbers on Everest, Lhotse and Nuptse pay a $600 icefall route fee from spring 2026. Waste rules now ask climbers to bring down 8 kg of rubbish, at least 2 kg of it from above Camp II.

items.title: Ski mountaineering makes its Olympic debut
items.text: Skimo was added to the Winter Olympics in Milan Cortina, with races in Bormio, Italy. Marianne Fatton of Switzerland and Oriol Cardona Coll of Spain won the first sprint titles.

items.title: Everest permit fee rises to $15,000
items.text: The fee for foreign climbers on the Nepal side went up from $11,000 to $15,000.

items.title: GPS tracking chips become compulsory on Everest
items.text: After a deadly 2023 season, Nepal's tourism department made tracking chips or GPS devices mandatory for climbers and guides, to make search and rescue quicker.

trends.title: More rules, fewer shortcuts
trends.text: Nepal has been tightening requirements around permits, tracking and waste. Reports also mention an experience requirement for Everest climbers; check the Department of Tourism for the current text before you plan a trip.

trends.title: Crowding
trends.text: Record permit numbers mean queues at the Hillary Step area and long waits at the top in good-weather windows. Guides argue for staggering summit days.

trends.title: Cleaner mountains
trends.text: Clean-up expeditions and 'carry out what you carry in' rules are now standard on the Nepal side.

trends.title: Technology
trends.text: Better forecasting, satellite messengers and lighter kit have changed how teams plan, though none of them replaces experience.
